subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram partial-stream finalization lacks clear delivery-mode observability (sent vs preview-finalized vs canceled)

question: Should this issue require a durable delivery-confirmation boundary for Telegram partial-stream finals, or is explicit dispatch logging and message hook parity sufficient?
rationale: The issue body asks for outcome observability, while the first comment asks for session delivery state not to imply platform delivery before the channel confirms send/edit success; that choice affects channel contracts, hooks, and transcript semantics.

options.title: Require delivery confirmation boundary
options.body: Treat Telegram send/edit confirmation as the point where final replies become delivered, and require the linked fix or successor to cover follow-up failures with tests and real Telegram proof.

options.title: Limit to logs and hooks
options.body: Add explicit outcome tags and hook parity while leaving session transcript generation separate from platform receipt.

options.title: Fold into cross-channel contract
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87561 as the owner for durable final delivery semantics, while keeping this issue as the Telegram-specific repro until the linked PR lands or is replaced.

recommendation.title: Require delivery confirmation boundary
recommendation.body: Treat Telegram send/edit confirmation as the point where final replies become delivered, and require the linked fix or successor to cover follow-up failures with tests and real Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: History shows the broadest and most recent ownership signals across the affected Telegram lane-delivery and dispatcher files.
